items.title: Anthropic ships Claude Dashboards and Motion — turn a data question into a live chart, no SQL
items.summary: Dashboards (beta, paid plans) connects to BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, or Salesforce — ask a plain-English question and Claude writes the query, builds a live chart, and keeps it refreshed as the data changes. Motion (beta, Team/Enterprise) turns a report or chart into a short animation written as editable code, exported as MP4. Docs, Slides, and Design also left beta the same day, free on every plan.
items.why: This is Claude quietly turning into a full data workspace — a live chart wired to your actual warehouse from a plain-English question, not a one-off script you have to babysit.
items.action: Point Dashboards at a spreadsheet or small table from a side project and ask it a plain-English question — then check whether the query it wrote is one you'd actually trust.

items.title: Snyk put a LangGraph agent in its core product — 60K+ queries, 85%+ resolved without a ticket
items.summary: Snyk Assist runs on a single LangGraph runtime behind Slack, a web app, and a panel in Snyk's core product, with LangChain middleware for guardrails/fallbacks, a Postgres checkpointer for multi-turn memory, and LangSmith for tracing, CI-gated offline evals, and scheduled online evals in production.
items.why: This is the concrete shape of a production agent — one runtime, real evals gating deploys, real numbers — not a demo.
items.action: If your agent evals are still ad hoc, borrow the CI-gating pattern here: offline evals block the pull request, scheduled online evals watch production after it ships.
